understanding: Invoke-BacklogStateReaper (lib/backlog-state-reaper.ps1) is a pure read-only proposer that takes an $Items array, finds orphaned 'running'/'working' tasks (dead agent_pid + no fresh heartbeat + no matching runtime state), and recovers them to 'approved' (or 'held' after MaxZombieRetries) at lines ~283-305. The bug: a parent that already finished decomposition (its 8 child-atoms exist) was still 'running' (its worker died before driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1 could flip it to status='decomposed'). The reaper saw 'running' + dead pid and recovered it to 'approved', so on re-claim the whole parent re-runs heavy synthesis and spawns duplicate children. Fix: before recovering an orphan, detect whether it is an already-decomposed parent (has children with parent_id==its id, OR carries a decomposed marker) and, if so, flip it to status='decomposed' instead of re-queueing it.
summary: Add a single guard at the top of the recovery block (after the existing liveness/heartbeat/runtime guards, before the approved/held computation). Precompute once, before the foreach, a case-insensitive HashSet of every parent_id (and canary_gate_parent_id) present in the passed-in $Items — which IS the full backlog, since the driver calls the reaper with $items = @(Get-Backlog). For each orphan, if its id is in that set OR it already carries a truthy 'decomposed' marker, set status='decomposed' with a recovered_reason, record it in the 'recovered' bucket (so the existing driver's Save-Backlog persists the flip), and skip the approved/held recovery and zombie_recovery_count bump entirely. Leaf atoms (no children, no marker) keep today's behavior verbatim. Add a ParseFile/smoke check plus unit tests for (a) orphan-with-children→decomposed, (b) orphan-with-decomposed-marker→decomposed, (c) orphan-leaf→approved as before, and a guard that a live/heartbeat-fresh parent is still preserved untouched.

decision_atoms.statement: Detect children by scanning the already-passed $Items array (build a parent-id set once before the loop), NOT by calling Get-Backlog inside the reaper.
decision_atoms.reason: driver.ps1:503 invokes the reaper as $items = @(Get-Backlog) inside Invoke-BacklogLocked, so $Items already contains the full, lock-consistent backlog including every child. Scanning it reuses the data Get-Backlog produced (honoring Foundation #2 'no new mechanism') while keeping the function pure and testable; calling Get-Backlog internally would break the existing Items-based unit tests, add a hidden global dependency, and risk reentrancy under the held backlog lock.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Diverges from the literal wording of the contract hint ('use Get-Backlog'). If a future caller ever passes only the single zombie item rather than the whole backlog, the child scan finds nothing — mitigated by the advanced version's optional Get-Backlog fallback.

decision_atoms.statement: Precompute the set of all non-blank parent_id (+ canary_gate_parent_id) values across $Items once, before the foreach, into a HashSet[string] with OrdinalIgnoreCase; ignore self-referential parent_id==own-id.
decision_atoms.reason: Turns an otherwise O(n^2) per-orphan rescan into a single O(n) prepass; case-insensitive ordinal matching mirrors the existing id comparisons in Test-BacklogStateReaperMatchingRuntimeState; excluding self-references prevents a degenerate item from marking itself as its own parent.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Reads parent linkage from the input items eagerly even in the common case where no orphans exist; negligible for realistic backlog sizes (tens to low hundreds of items).

decision_atoms.statement: Place the decomposed-parent check INSIDE the recovery block, after the $livePid/$freshWorkerHeartbeat/$matchingRuntime guard (the 'continue' at ~line 281), not before it.
decision_atoms.reason: A parent with a live worker still mid-decomposition must not be sidelined; the task's 'before recovery' means before the approved/held assignment, which is exactly this position. Only genuinely orphaned parents reach this code.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: None of substance — this is the only placement that both fixes the bug and leaves live decomposing workers untouched.

decision_atoms.statement: Record the running->decomposed flip in the 'recovered' bucket (with to_status='decomposed' and a distinct recovered_reason), not in 'preserved'.
decision_atoms.reason: The driver persists only when @($r.recovered).Count -gt 0 (driver.ps1:506). If the decomposed flip went to 'preserved', Save-Backlog would not run when it is the only change in a cycle, so the item would stay 'running' in backlog.jsonl and be re-evaluated forever. Putting it in 'recovered' guarantees persistence and keeps the action auditable.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Semantically 'recovered' connotes 'requeued for retry', whereas this is 'sidelined as already-done'; the distinct to_status='decomposed' and reason string disambiguate it in the evidence/audit trail.

decision_atoms.statement: Treat children-existence as the primary, authoritative signal and the 'decomposed' field/tag marker as a secondary OR fallback; use status='decomposed' as the resulting status to match the existing convention.
decision_atoms.reason: Physically-present children are unambiguous proof decomposition happened. driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1:193 already closes parents via Set-Idea -Status 'decomposed', so reusing that exact status keeps the claim picker (which excludes non-running/approved statuses) from ever re-selecting the task and avoids inventing a new state.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: The exact within-item 'marker' field name is not fully pinned down (status='decomposed' parents are already filtered out earlier as 'status-not-governed'), so the marker branch is defensive; the children check carries the real weight.

assumptions: The reaper is always invoked with the full backlog as $Items (verified at driver.ps1:502-505 where $items = @(Get-Backlog) is passed under the backlog lock).
Children link to their parent via a 'parent_id' field equal to the parent's id; 'canary_gate_parent_id' is a known sibling field worth matching too (lib/backlog-core.ps1, lib/backlog-workpack.ps1).

The canonical 'decomposed' marker is status='decomposed' (driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1:193); since this recovery block only governs 'running'/'working' items, the within-item marker check targets a separate truthy field (e.g. 'decomposed'/'decomposed_at') and is a belt-and-suspenders complement to the children check.

An orphan that is itself a parent should be flipped to 'decomposed' regardless of how many children exist (>=1 child is sufficient evidence; the reaper does not need the completion-check's >= ceil(expected/2) quorum).
Flipping to 'decomposed' should NOT increment zombie_recovery_count, since this is not a retry.

risks.risk: Marker field-name mismatch: the within-item 'decomposed' marker may be stored under a different key than assumed, so the marker branch silently never fires.
risks.mitigation: Rely on the children-existence check as the primary signal (it does not depend on any marker), and read the marker via the existing Get-BacklogStateReaperObjectValue with a small candidate-name list ('decomposed','is_decomposed','decomposed_at') so adding another alias later is trivial.

risks.risk: Child-detection convention divergence: driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1 detects children via the 'decomposed-child' tag + parent_id-in-text, while the crusher/contract uses parent_id; matching only one convention could miss children.
risks.mitigation: Match both 'parent_id' and 'canary_gate_parent_id' for the structured link (the reliable machine field); document that the tag/text convention is a recognized alternate and can be added to the prepass if a real case surfaces.

risks.risk: Persistence regression: if the flip is mis-bucketed into 'preserved', Save-Backlog never runs for a decomposed-only cycle and the 'running' line lingers.
risks.mitigation: Explicitly add the item to the 'recovered' list and assert in a unit test that result.recovered contains an entry with to_status='decomposed' for the parent.

risks.risk: Sidelining a live decomposing parent if the check is placed before the liveness guard.
risks.mitigation: Insert the check strictly after the existing $livePid/$freshWorkerHeartbeat/$matchingRuntime 'continue'; add a unit/guard case asserting a live-pid parent-with-children is preserved unchanged.

risks.risk: Control-plane change to the autonomous queue governor could mis-sideline a legitimately-incomplete parent and strand its work.
risks.mitigation: Gate the flip on concrete evidence (>=1 actual child item OR explicit marker); leaf atoms are provably untouched; ship with the required ParseFile/smoke + the (a)/(b)/(c) unit tests and a critic pass before wiring.

minimal_version: In Invoke-BacklogStateReaper, before the foreach, build $parentIdsWithChildren = a HashSet[string] (OrdinalIgnoreCase) of every non-blank parent_id/canary_gate_parent_id in $Items, excluding self-references. Inside the recovery block, immediately after the liveness/heartbeat/runtime 'continue' guard, add: if $parentIdsWithChildren.Contains($id) OR the item has a truthy 'decomposed' marker, then Set status='decomposed', set recovered_reason=("zombie-{status}: already decomposed (children/marker present) -- not re-queued to avoid duplicate synthesis"), set recovered_at, add the copy to $resultItems, push an entry to $recovered with from_status=$status/to_status='decomposed'/recovered_reason, and 'continue' (skipping the priorRecoveries/zombie_recovery_count and approved/held logic). Everything else (leaf-atom path) is unchanged. Add a ParseFile/AST smoke check and three unit tests: (a) orphan running parent with a child item (parent_id==parent.id) -> status='decomposed', not approved/held, present in recovered with to_status='decomposed'; (b) orphan with truthy 'decomposed' marker, no children -> status='decomposed'; (c) orphan leaf, no children/marker -> status='approved' (recovery 1/2), exactly as today.
advanced_version: All of the minimal version, plus: (1) add a small private helper Test-BacklogStateReaperHasChildren / Get-BacklogStateReaperParentIdSet that also recognizes the 'decomposed-child' tag + parent-id-in-text convention used by driver/86-loop-completion-checks.ps1, so both linkage styles are covered; (2) add an optional -AllItems (or -Children) parameter that, when supplied, is used for the child scan instead of $Items, with a guarded fallback to Get-Backlog only if both -AllItems is absent AND $Items appears to be a single-item slice and Get-Backlog is available — preserving purity in the common path while staying correct if a future caller passes only the zombie; (3) emit a structured evidence entry (e.g. evidence.decomposed_parents_sidelined with id + child_count) for observability; (4) add the success-test #4 regression as an integration test: reap the orphaned parent, then run the claim picker over result.items and assert it selects none of the sidelined parents and that no duplicate child atoms are created.
